run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T01:10:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by two simultaneous rollout restarts of its dependencies. Deployments ad and payment were restarted at 01:09:06Z and 01:09:05Z (new ReplicaSets carrying kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, previous pods killed 01:09:08/01:09:09Z). Neither pod template has a readiness probe, so the replacement pods were counted Ready as soon as their containers started and served Service traffic while their applications were not yet listening; both were also almost permanently CPU-throttled (ad limits 50m/450Mi, throttled ~96-99% of CFS periods; payment limits 20m/160Mi, throttled ~94-96%). The new ad container started 01:09:08Z but only logged 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 01:15:28Z; the new payment container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 01:10:30Z. Frontend error spans were exactly zero before 01:10:09Z, then rose on two paths only: GET /api/data -> grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (417.9 error spans in 01:10-01:20) and POST /api/checkout -> grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (75.8). The failures are caller-side connection failures: frontend attempted 417.9 failing GetAds calls while ad service recorded 0 error spans, and checkout recorded 75.8 failing Charge client spans while payment recorded 0 error spans and logged successful 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs. frontend error spans returned to 0 by 01:20:09Z. Deployment ad is named as root cause because the GetAds path dominates frontend error volume and lasted longest; Deployment payment was restarted the same way and produced the second, smaller checkout path. The flagd flags adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on remain a hypothesis only: they declare faults on the same two paths, but ad and payment themselves returned no application errors and traffic recovered while those flags still read 'on'. An unrelated fraud-detection container OOMKill at 01:10:52Z was also observed but is not tied to this alert.

claims.text: Frontend span error rate was zero at every 2-minute increase sample from 00:49:09Z through 01:08:09Z, first became non-zero at 01:10:09Z (57.3 error spans per 2m), peaked at 965.3 at 01:12:09Z, and was back to 0 at 01:20:09Z and 01:21:09Z (the last samples available, data_as_of 01:21:09Z).

In the 10 minutes 01:10:00Z-01:20:00Z the frontend service recorded 1987.4 spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 29386.3 spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation, not requests).

The frontend error spans are confined to two call paths in 01:10-01:20: GET /api/data and its grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client span (417.9 error spans each), POST /api/checkout and its grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span (75.8 error spans each), plus tcp.connect (12.6 error spans).

The failed calls never reached the dependencies as errors: in 01:10-01:20 frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had 417.9 ERROR and 140 UNSET spans while service ad's server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had 137.4 UNSET and zero ERROR; checkout's client span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had 75.8 ERROR and 332.6 UNSET while service payment's server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had 321.6 UNSET and zero ERROR.

At 01:09:05Z-01:09:09Z Deployments payment and ad scaled up new ReplicaSets payment-5d565cf9b and ad-5f8dd7c58d, created pods payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn and ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5, and killed the previous pods payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp (01:09:09Z) and ad-554b849958-6z62j (01:09:08Z); all these events are Normal.

Deployment ad and Deployment payment were rollout-restarted: the new ReplicaSet pod templates carry kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt 2026-11-17T01:09:06Z (ad-5f8dd7c58d) and 2026-11-17T01:09:05Z (payment-5d565cf9b), and the previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 carry no such annotation.

Apart from the restartedAt annotation the old and new ReplicaSet pod templates for ad and payment are identical in the visible fields: same image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-payment), same env, ports, securityContext, restartPolicy and same container resources (ad limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi; payment limits cpu 20m / memory 160Mi).

Neither the ad nor the payment container in otel-demo defines a readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe (readiness null, liveness null, startup null in the pod spec and in both ReplicaSet templates).
The replacement ad container in pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 started at 01:09:08Z but logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 01:13:48Z and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 01:15:28Z.
The replacement payment pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 01:10:30Z.

The new ad container was CPU-throttled for 96.6%-98.8% of CFS periods from 01:10Z to 01:19Z, versus 7.3%-8.0% for the previous ad pod ad-554b849958-6z62j; the new payment container was throttled 93.6%-95.6% at 01:10-01:12Z versus 8.8%-12.2% for the previous payment pod.

ad service server spans for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds fell to 0 in the 2-minute increase samples at 01:13:00Z, 01:15:00Z, 01:17:00Z and 01:19:00Z and resumed at 01:21:00Z (113.04 spans, status STATUS_CODE_UNSET).

Once listening, the new ad pod handled requests: its logs from 01:18:26Z to 01:18:53Z show 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' and 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.' lines.
The new payment pod logged successful transactions ('Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.') from 01:13:20Z-01:13:28Z and again 01:17:13Z-01:18:46Z.

Service checkout shows its own error spans in the same window, on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (both 83.7 per 2m at 01:13:00Z, 42.7 at 01:15:00Z, 0 from 01:17:00Z).

Other frontend dependencies showed no rise in error spans during the burst: accounting, ad, fraud-detection and payment 0 ERROR spans per 2m, and recommendation only background-level 1.33 (also present at 01:07Z, before the deviation); frontend-proxy's own error spans rose from a pre-burst 1.33 per 2m to 466.7 at 01:12Z and 242.7 at 01:19Z.

Separately from the rollouts, the fraud-detection container in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n79gv was terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at 01:10:52Z (started 00:38:05Z), restartCount 1, restarted at 01:10:53Z; its Deployment is generation 1 with a 400Mi memory limit.

ConfigMap flagd-config currently holds fault-injection flags adFailure defaultVariant 'on' ('Fail ad service') and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant 'on' ('Payment service is unavailable'), with every other fault flag (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) set to 'off'.
Services ad, payment and frontend are ClusterIP services with selectors matching their pod labels and port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, i.e. no service-level port or selector mismatch was found.

The rollout restarts are the origin of the frontend failures: because Deployment ad and Deployment payment define no readiness probe, the replacement pods were admitted to their Service endpoints as soon as the containers started, the previous serving pods were deleted at 01:09:08/01:09:09Z, and the heavily CPU-throttled replacement containers were not yet listening (ad until 01:15:28Z, payment until 01:10:30Z); frontend GetAds and checkout Charge connections therefore failed until the new processes were listening plus a client reconnection delay.

The frontend GetAds errors that continued after ad logged 'listening' at 01:15:28Z (until about 01:19Z) and the checkout Charge errors that continued after payment logged 'listening' at 01:10:30Z (until about 01:15Z) are gRPC client channel reconnect/backoff delays after connection failures, not continued server-side errors.

The fault-injection flags adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on in ConfigMap flagd-config are a candidate cause because their declared faults ('Fail ad service', 'Payment service is unavailable') name the same two failing call paths seen from frontend and checkout; their value at the time of the incident cannot be determined from the current ConfigMap state.

Neither dependency produced application-level errors during the burst: ad service's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server span had zero ERROR status, ad pod logs show normal 'Targeted/Non-targeted ad request received' responses, and payment logged 'Charge request received.' with 'Transaction complete.' for its charges, so the observed failure mode is unavailability at the caller, not a failing ad or payment implementation.

The flagd fault flags being 'on' does not by itself explain this incident: frontend's ERROR increase had already returned to 0 at 01:20:09Z and 01:21:09Z, and ad served 113.04 oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no ERROR in the 01:19-01:21 window.

A pod-spec change such as a new image, new env or different resource limits introduced by the 01:09 rollouts was considered and rejected as the trigger: the previous and new ReplicaSet pod templates are identical for image, env, ports, securityContext and container resources, and differ only by the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation.

The fraud-detection OOMKill at 01:10:52Z was considered as a cause of the frontend error rate and rejected: fraud-detection recorded 0 ERROR spans in 01:05-01:25 and the frontend's failing paths are the ad and payment client calls, while checkout's errors are on its PaymentService/Charge client span.

Add a readinessProbe (gRPC health check or TCP 8080) to Deployment ad and Deployment payment so replacement pods are not added to their Service endpoints before the application listens, and raise their CPU limits (currently 50m for ad and 20m for payment) since both replacement containers were CPU-throttled for ~94-99% of CFS periods while starting.

Identify who or what issued the rollout restarts of Deployment ad at 01:09:06Z and Deployment payment at 01:09:05Z using cluster audit logs or CI/CD history, and review whether the fault-injection flags adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on in ConfigMap flagd-config are intentional.

Treat the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart (exit 137 at 01:10:52Z under a 400Mi limit) as a separate item to investigate; it is not tied to the frontend RequestErrorRate signal in the evidence gathered.

gaps: Jaeger returned no traces for the incident window: a frontend trace search over 01:09:00Z-01:21:00Z returned nothing and the newest frontend spans the backend returned were from 00:53:38Z-00:53:42Z, so the exact gRPC status code/message (e.g. UNAVAILABLE vs DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) and parent-child reconstruction for the failing calls are unknown.

The frontend container produced no readable stdout/stderr lines for the entire authorized window (0 lines, 0 bytes; queried with and without an error filter), so any client-side error text from the frontend is unknown.

A filtered query on the new ad pod for error/fail/exception/flag/grpc/GetAds returned no matching lines (status no_data) and a query on the fraud-detection pod for error/fail/panic/restart/OOM/killed likewise returned nothing, so the absence of error text in those pods' logs is not established.

The actor or mechanism that triggered the 01:09:05Z/01:09:06Z rollout restarts is unknown: only the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt template annotations and the controller events are visible, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
The flagd-config values during 01:10-01:19Z are unknown; the ConfigMap was read at query time (about 01:29Z) and objects reflect current state only.

kube-state-metrics series were not returned for this target: queries of kube_.* metric names, kube_pod_container_info and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="otel-demo"} all returned no data, so deployment ready-replica history and image digests of the old pods are unknown.
The networkpolicies query for otel-demo matched nothing; absence of NetworkPolicies is therefore not established.
No previous container instance logs were available for the restarted fraud-detection pod (HTTP 400 previous terminated container not found), so why its memory reached the 400Mi limit is unknown.
Metric data for traces_span_metrics_calls_total ends at data_as_of 01:21:09Z, so frontend error behavior after 01:21Z and the alert's current state at 01:28:57Z are unknown.
The alert's rule definition could not be read: list_prometheus_rules for RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the exact alerting expression and its window are unknown.
next_steps: Pull cluster audit logs / GitOps or CI history for the 01:09:05Z-01:09:06Z window to identify who restarted Deployment ad and Deployment payment.
Review whether ConfigMap flagd-config flags adFailure and paymentUnreachable should be 'on' in this environment, and capture their values from a source with historical retention.
Add and validate readinessProbes (gRPC health or TCP 8080) and raise CPU limits for ad and payment in a staging rollout to confirm the startup gap disappears.
Investigate the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart (400Mi limit) separately, including its memory usage trend before 01:10:52Z.
